Philosophical Roots and Early Foundations
The origins of Information Science are deeply rooted in the philosophies of the Enlightenment, a
period that championed knowledge, education, and the accessibility of information as essential
drivers of human progress. Thinkers of the Enlightenment believed in the transformative power of
information, emphasizing its role in fostering democracy, innovation, and societal improvement.
Leaders such as Thomas Jefferson embodied this philosophy, recognizing the critical role of
libraries and information systems in supporting democratic principles. Jefferson’s vision underscored
the necessity of accessible, organized repositories of knowledge for informed citizenry. This
emphasis laid the groundwork for institutional developments in the 19th century that would shape the
future of the field.

libraries and information systems in supporting democratic principles. Jefferson’s vision underscored
the necessity of accessible, organized repositories of knowledge for informed citizenry. This
emphasis laid the groundwork for institutional developments in the 19th century that would shape the
